sections.label: Carbon tax introduction
sections.summary: A carbon tax is introduced as part of an approach to improve energy efficiency and address climate change commitments.

sentences.speaker: The Minister for Finance (Mr Heng Swee Keat)
sentences.text: The introduction of a carbon tax is part of an overall approach to improve Singapore’s energy efficiency and address our climate change commitments.

sections.label: Increased social spending areas
sections.summary: The Government has substantially increased social spending in education, healthcare, housing, Workfare and Silver Support.

sentences.speaker: The Minister for Finance (Mr Heng Swee Keat)
sentences.text: The Government has substantially increased social spending in major areas, including education, healthcare, housing, Workfare and Silver Support.

sections.label: Tightening fiscal position, GST increase
sections.summary: Rising expenditures, falling corporate tax rates and international tax discussions lead to steps to strengthen revenue, including a GST increase.

sentences.speaker: The Minister for Finance (Mr Heng Swee Keat)
sentences.text: Our fiscal position is expected to tighten considerably in the coming years due to rising expenditures, especially in healthcare, infrastructure and security.

sentences.speaker: The Minister for Finance (Mr Heng Swee Keat)
sentences.text: Several countries are moving to reduce their corporate income tax rates.

sentences.speaker: The Minister for Finance (Mr Heng Swee Keat)
sentences.text: There are also ongoing discussions to develop international tax rules under the Base Erosion and Profit Shifting project.

sentences.speaker: The Minister for Finance (Mr Heng Swee Keat)
sentences.text: This is why we are taking steps to strengthen our revenue position, including through an increase in the Goods and Services Tax.

sections.label: Managing expenditure and infrastructure funding
sections.summary: Expenditure growth will be managed carefully, with new funding approaches explored for large-scale infrastructure through borrowing by Statutory Boards and Government-owned companies.

sentences.speaker: The Minister for Finance (Mr Heng Swee Keat)
sentences.text: We will do this by managing our expenditure growth carefully and continually seeking more cost-effective solutions in the public sector.

sentences.speaker: The Minister for Finance (Mr Heng Swee Keat)
sentences.text: We will explore new funding approaches for large-scale infrastructure investments, particularly through borrowing by Statutory Boards and Government-owned companies.

sections.label: Reserves framework and returns
sections.summary: The Reserves help weather shocks and build confidence, and the framework for investing them and using part of returns will continue.

sentences.speaker: The Minister for Finance (Mr Heng Swee Keat)
sentences.text: Our Reserves provide us with the means to weather shocks and crises and strengthen investor and market confidence in Singapore.

sentences.speaker: The Minister for Finance (Mr Heng Swee Keat)
sentences.text: We will continue to uphold the framework that enables us to invest our Reserves for long-term returns, and to use part of the returns to supplement our budgetary needs.
